structurally_unverifiable.reason: their source document prints imperial units only, with no metric equivalent to cross-check against. PERMANENT - collecting more text cannot raise it.

limitations: VERIFICATION IS A PROPERTY OF THE DOCUMENT, NOT THE UNIT, AND THE CEILING IS PERMANENT. 36 CFR 1191 prints every dimension twice and verifies at 258/261 = 98.9%. OSHA (29 CFR 1910, 1926) and HUD (24 CFR 3280) print imperial only and verify at 7/311 = 2.3% - in BOTH units. So 311 of 572 rules (54.4%) are STRUCTURALLY unverifiable by the dual-unit cross-check: their source prints no metric equivalent, and no amount of further collecting can raise that. It is a structural ceiling, not a sample-size problem. The per-unit figures (in 60%, ft 4.3%) are themselves an aggregate hiding this - feet look unverifiable only because 132 of the 140 foot rules come from imperial-only documents; inside 36 CFR 1191 feet verify at 4/5. Practical consequence for a consumer: treat 36 CFR 1191 rules as cross-checked and every other document's rules as parsed-but-unconfirmed, and weight a compliance finding accordingly.

COVERAGE, MEASURED 2026-08-27 (not estimated): the eCFR search API reports 2,957 sections CFR-wide carrying the dual-unit dimensional pattern, across 230 parts, with count relation 'eq' (not a capped 'gte'). The 7 parts harvested here hold 185 of them = 6.3%. BUT that denominator is dimensional prose in general, not building rules - the largest holders are fisheries (50 CFR 648), endangered species, hazmat shipping and consumer appliances. Filtering the 223 unharvested parts by building-related headings leaves 23 parts / 148 sections, and most of those are vehicles (46 CFR vessel construction, 49 CFR 38 and 36 CFR 1192 transportation) or nuclear (10 CFR 50). Genuinely building-relevant and still missing: 28 CFR 36 (DOJ ADA Title III), 36 CFR 1190 (PROWAG, public right-of-way), 36 CFR 1234 (records storage facilities), 16 CFR 1211 (residential garage door operators), 7 CFR 1924 (construction and repair). So coverage of BUILDING dimensional CFR is high, and 6.3% understates it - but the honest figure is 'high', not 'complete', and the remaining candidates are named above rather than left as an unbounded gap.

eCFR XML only. UFC and ADA PDFs are NOT parsed - they carry no machine-readable section tree, so any citation from them would be reconstructed rather than sourced. That is 169 UFC PDFs (679 MB) and 2 ADA PDFs whose rule content is entirely unmeasured - unlike the CFR gap above, this one has NO number attached to it yet.
Subject extraction is shallow (text before 'shall'). Every rule carries its verbatim quote so a human can check what was read.
Applicability/scope is NOT modelled. A rule knows its section and heading, not which building types or occupancies it governs.
Permissive, conditional and exception clauses are quarantined, not interpreted. Some of them ARE requirements under conditions.
No rule here has been evaluated against a real reconstructed plan.

rules.subject: This safety trip

rules.subject: When slashers are operated by control levers, these levers
rules.quote: When slashers are operated by control levers, these levers shall be connected to a horizontal bar or treadle located not more than 69 inches above the floor to control the operation from any point.

rules.subject: Where a noncontinuous connection is used, the supply line
rules.quote: Where a noncontinuous connection is used, the supply line shall terminate at a point not less than 2 inches (5 cm) above the regularly provided opening for filling so that the water can be observed as it enters the generator.

rules.subject: Where practicable, all combustibles
rules.quote: Where practicable, all combustibles shall be relocated at least 35 feet (10.7 m) from the work site.

rules.subject: bottom of the overhead folders
rules.quote: The bottom of the overhead folders shall be located not less than 7 feet from the floor or working surface.

rules.subject: chipper spout
rules.quote: The chipper spout shall be enclosed to a height of not less than 36 inches from the floor or the operator's platform.

rules.subject: electric detonator is preferable for firing; if a fuse is used, it
rules.quote: An electric detonator is preferable for firing; if a fuse is used, it shall be an approved safety fuse with a burning rate of not less than 120 seconds per yard and a minimum length of 3 feet, in accordance with Safety in the Handling and Use of Explosives, IME Pamphlet No.

rules.subject: gas bell
rules.quote: The gas bell shall move freely without tendency to bind and shall have a clearance of at least 2 inches (5 cm) from the shell.

rules.subject: in-mask sampling device (probe)
rules.quote: The in-mask sampling device (probe) shall be designed and used so that the air sample is drawn from the breathing zone of the test subject, midway between the nose and mouth and with the probe extending into the facepiece cavity at least 1/4 inch.

rules.subject: minimum clear space between the lower and upper bunk
rules.quote: The minimum clear space between the lower and upper bunk shall be not less than 27 inches.

rules.subject: minimum vertical clearance between sprinklers and material below
rules.quote: The minimum vertical clearance between sprinklers and material below shall be 18 inches (45.7 cm).

rules.subject: outlet
rules.quote: The outlet shall be at least 3 feet (0.9 m) from combustible construction.

rules.subject: table throat opening
rules.quote: The table throat opening shall be not more than 2 1/2 inches when tables are set or aligned with each other for zero cut.

rules.subject: test operator
rules.quote: The test operator shall begin at least 12 inches from the facepiece and move the smoke stream around the whole perimeter of the mask.

rules.subject: top rods
rules.quote: The top rods shall be not more than 72 inches above the level on which the operator stands.

rules.subject: width of openings in the grates
rules.quote: The width of openings in the grates shall be a maximum of 2 1/2 inches (6.35 cm).

rules.subject: (vii) Hoods for horizontal single-spindle disc grinders
rules.quote: (vii) Hoods for horizontal single-spindle disc grinders shall be constructed to conform as closely as possible to the hood shown in figure D-57.6. It is essential that there be a space between the back of the wheel and the hood, and a space around the periphery of the wheel of at least 1 inch (2.54 cm) in order to permit the suction to act around the wheel periphery.

rules.subject: In booths where the open front is the only exit, such exits
rules.quote: In booths where the open front is the only exit, such exits shall be not less than 3 feet (0.912 m) wide.

rules.subject: (11) Each service or fueling area
rules.quote: (11) Each service or fueling area shall be provided with at least one fire extinguisher having a rating of not less than 20-B:C located so that an extinguisher will be within 75 feet of each pump, dispenser, underground fill pipe opening, and lubrication or service area.

rules.subject: (11) Inside of buildings, cylinders
rules.quote: (11) Inside of buildings, cylinders shall be stored in a well-protected, well-ventilated, dry location, at least 20 feet (6.1 m) from highly combustible materials such as oil or excelsior.

rules.subject: (13) For temporary heating, heaters (other than integral heater-container units)
rules.quote: (13) For temporary heating, heaters (other than integral heater-container units) shall be located at least 6 feet from any LP-Gas container.

rules.subject: (2) Driveways between and around combustible storage piles
rules.quote: (2) Driveways between and around combustible storage piles shall be at least 15 feet wide and maintained free from accumulation of rubbish, equipment, or other articles or materials.

rules.subject: (2) Each end of “LH” and “DLH” series steel joists and steel joist girders
rules.quote: (2) Each end of “LH” and “DLH” series steel joists and steel joist girders shall be attached to the support structure with a minimum of two 1/4-inch (6 mm) fillet welds 2 inches (51 mm) long, or with two 3/4-inch (19 mm) bolts, or the equivalent.

rules.subject: (2) Filling of portable containers or containers mounted on skids from storage containers
rules.quote: (2) Filling of portable containers or containers mounted on skids from storage containers shall be performed not less than 50 feet from the nearest building.

rules.quote: (2) Special decompression chamber. (i) The headroom in the special decompression chamber shall be not less than a minimum 7 feet and the cubical content shall provide at least 50 cubic feet of airspace for each employee.

rules.subject: (2) The employer
rules.quote: (2) The employer shall ensure that there is in the vicinity of each barge in use at least one U.S. Coast Guard-approved 30-inch lifering with not less than 90 feet of line attached, and at least one portable or permanent ladder which will reach the top of the apron to the surface of the water.

rules.subject: (3) Container safety relief devices and regulator relief vents
rules.quote: (3) Container safety relief devices and regulator relief vents shall be located not less than 5 feet in any direction from air openings into sealed combustion system appliances or mechanical ventilation air intakes.

rules.subject: (3) Guardrail systems
rules.quote: (3) Guardrail systems shall be capable of withstanding, without failure, a force of at least 200 pounds (890 N) applied within 2 inches (5.1 cm) of the top edge, in any outward or downward direction, at any point along the top edge.

rules.subject: (3) Manual force used to move the scaffold
rules.quote: (3) Manual force used to move the scaffold shall be applied as close to the base as practicable, but not more than 5 feet (1.5 m) above the supporting surface.

rules.subject: (3) The fulcrum point of outrigger beams
rules.quote: (3) The fulcrum point of outrigger beams shall rest on secure bearings at least 6 inches (15.2 cm) in each horizontal dimension.

rules.subject: (3) The storage area
rules.quote: (3) The storage area shall be graded in a manner to divert possible spills away from buildings or other exposures, or shall be surrounded by a curb or earth dike at least 12 inches high.

rules.subject: (3) Toeboards
rules.quote: (3) Toeboards shall be a minimum of 3 1/2 inches (9 cm) in vertical height from their top edge to the level of the walking/working surface.

rules.subject: (4) Fire hose
rules.quote: (4) Fire hose shall be at least 1 1/2 inches in nominal diameter; the water pressure shall at all times be adequate for efficient operation of the type of nozzle used; and the water supply shall be such as to ensure an uninterrupted flow.

rules.subject: (4) Heaters used in the vicinity of combustible tarpaulins, canvas, or similar coverings
rules.quote: (4) Heaters used in the vicinity of combustible tarpaulins, canvas, or similar coverings shall be located at least 10 feet from the coverings.

rules.subject: (4) Ropes

rules.subject: (4) Stairtowers (scaffold stairway/towers)
rules.quote: (4) Stairtowers (scaffold stairway/towers) shall be positioned such that their bottom step is not more than 24 inches (61 cm.) above the scaffold supporting level.

rules.subject: (4) The operator's station of a hoisting machine
rules.quote: (4) The operator's station of a hoisting machine shall be provided with overhead protection equivalent to tight planking not less than 2 inches thick.

rules.subject: (4) Vertical pickups
rules.quote: (4) Vertical pickups shall be spaced not more than 50 feet apart.

rules.subject: (5) Clearance of at least 36 inches

rules.quote: (9) Connections between safety net panels shall be as strong as integral net components and shall be spaced not more than 6 inches (15 cm) apart.

rules.quote: (B) Normal vents shall be sized either in accordance with: (1) The American Petroleum Institute Standard 2000 (1968), Venting Atmospheric and Low-Pressure Storage Tanks; or (2) other accepted standard; or (3) shall be at least as large as the filling or withdrawal connection, whichever is larger but in no case less than 1 1/4 inch (3.175 cm) nominal inside diameter.

rules.subject: (E) Filling and emptying connections which are made and broken
rules.quote: (E) Filling and emptying connections which are made and broken shall be located outside of buildings at a location free from any source of ignition and not less than 5 feet (1.52 m) away from any building opening.

rules.subject: (F) Filling and emptying connections which are made and broken
rules.quote: (F) Filling and emptying connections which are made and broken shall be located outside of buildings at a location free from any source of ignition and not less than 5 feet (1.52 m) away from any building opening.

rules.subject: (G) The inlet of the fill pipe
rules.quote: (G) The inlet of the fill pipe shall be located outside of buildings at a location free from any source of ignition and not less than 5 feet (1.52 m) away from any building opening.

rules.subject: (c) Ring buoys with at least 90 feet of line
rules.quote: (c) Ring buoys with at least 90 feet of line shall be provided and readily available for emergency rescue operations.

rules.subject: (c) Whenever a shaft is used, it
rules.quote: (c) Whenever a shaft is used, it shall be provided, where space permits, with a safe, proper, and suitable staircase for its entire length, including landing platforms, not more than 20 feet apart.

rules.subject: (e) Permanent underground storage magazines
rules.quote: (e) Permanent underground storage magazines shall be at least 300 feet from any shaft, adit, or active underground working area.

rules.subject: (e) Planks
rules.quote: (e) Planks shall be laid together over solid bearings with the ends overlapping at least 1 foot.

rules.subject: (h) Every motor vehicle or conveyance used for transporting explosives
rules.quote: (h) Every motor vehicle or conveyance used for transporting explosives shall be marked or placarded on both sides, the front, and the rear with the word “Explosives” in red letters, not less than 4 inches in height, on white background.

rules.subject: (h) The minimum length of safety fuse to be used in blasting
rules.quote: (h) The minimum length of safety fuse to be used in blasting shall be as required by State law, but shall not be less than 30 inches.

rules.subject: (i) Acceptable wooden storage cabinets
rules.quote: (i) Acceptable wooden storage cabinets shall be constructed in the following manner, or equivalent: The bottom, sides, and top shall be constructed of an exterior grade of plywood at least 1 inch in thickness, which shall not break down or delaminate under standard fire test conditions.

rules.subject: (i) Bars
rules.quote: (i) Bars shall be not less than 2- by 4-inch wooden bars or the equivalent, located 2 feet from the hoistway line.

rules.subject: (i) Exhaust ducts
rules.quote: (i) Exhaust ducts shall be protected against mechanical damage and have a clearance from unprotected combustible construction or other combustible material of not less than 18 inches (45.72 cm).

rules.subject: (i) The maximum distance from the face for outrigger scaffolds
rules.quote: (i) The maximum distance from the face for outrigger scaffolds shall be 3 inches (8 cm);.

rules.subject: (i) The use of chlorinated solvents
rules.quote: (i) The use of chlorinated solvents shall be kept at least 200 feet, unless shielded, from the exposed arc, and surfaces prepared with chlorinated solvents shall be thoroughly dry before welding is permitted on such surfaces.

rules.subject: (i) When mechanical equipment is not being used, the warning line
rules.quote: (i) When mechanical equipment is not being used, the warning line shall be erected not less than 6 feet (1.8 m) from the roof edge.

rules.subject: (ii) All guards for inclined belts
rules.quote: (ii) All guards for inclined belts shall be arranged in such a manner that a minimum clearance of 7 feet (2.128 m) is maintained between belt and floor at any point outside of guard.

rules.subject: (ii) Buckles
rules.quote: (ii) Buckles shall be capable of withstanding an 8.9-kilonewton (2,000-pound-force) tension test with a maximum permanent deformation no greater than 0.4 millimeters (0.0156 inches).

rules.subject: (ii) Hook-on and attachable ladders
rules.quote: (ii) Hook-on and attachable ladders shall be positioned so that their bottom rung is not more than 24 inches (61 cm) above the scaffold supporting level;.

rules.subject: (ii) Posts
rules.quote: (ii) Posts shall be not more than 8 feet (2.432 m) apart; they are to be permanent and substantial, smooth, and free from protruding nails, bolts, and splinters.

rules.subject: (ii) The maximum distance from the face for plastering and lathing operations
rules.quote: (ii) The maximum distance from the face for plastering and lathing operations shall be 18 inches (46 cm).

rules.subject: (ii) The suspension wire rope
rules.quote: (ii) The suspension wire rope shall be covered with insulating material extending at least 4 feet (1.2 m) above the hoist.

rules.subject: (iii) After being erected, with the rope, wire, or chain attached, stanchions
rules.quote: (iii) After being erected, with the rope, wire, or chain attached, stanchions shall be capable of resisting, without tipping over, a force of at least 16 pounds (71 N) applied horizontally against the stanchion, 30 inches (.8 m) above the walking/working surface, perpendicular to the warning line, and in the direction of the floor, roof, or platform edge;.

rules.quote: (ix) Each scaffold stairway shall be at least 18 inches (45.7 cm) wide between stairrails.

rules.quote: (ix) The man lock shall be large enough so that those using it are not compelled to be in a cramped position, and shall not have less than 5 feet clear head room at the center and a minimum of 30 cubic feet of air space per occupant.

rules.subject: (k) Employee entrances to multi-story structures being demolished
rules.quote: (k) Employee entrances to multi-story structures being demolished shall be completely protected by sidewalk sheds or canopies, or both, providing protection from the face of the building for a minimum of 8 feet.

rules.subject: (k) In underground operations there
rules.quote: (k) In underground operations there shall be a “lightning” gap of at least 5 feet in the firing system ahead of the main firing switch; that is, between this switch and the source of power.

rules.quote: (s) Float (ship) scaffolds. (1) The platform shall be supported by a minimum of two bearers, each of which shall project a minimum of 6 inches (15.2 cm) beyond the platform on both sides.

rules.subject: (v) Each employee on a walkway located within a scaffold
rules.quote: (v) Each employee on a walkway located within a scaffold shall be protected by a guardrail system (with minimum 200 pound toprail capacity) installed within 9 1/2 inches (24.1 cm) of and along at least one side of the walkway.

rules.quote: (v) Hook-on and attachable ladders shall have a minimum rung length of 11 1/2 inches (29 cm); and.

rules.quote: (vi) A fire extinguisher, rated not less than 10B, shall be provided within 50 feet of wherever more than 5 gallons of flammable or combustible liquids or 5 pounds of flammable gas are being used on the jobsite.

rules.subject: (vi) Handrails, and toprails that are used as handrails,
rules.quote: (vi) Handrails, and toprails that are used as handrails, shall be at least 3 inches (7.6 cm) from other objects.

rules.subject: (vi) Hook-on and attachable ladders
rules.quote: (vi) Hook-on and attachable ladders shall have uniformly spaced rungs with a maximum spacing between rungs of 16 3/4 inches.

rules.subject: (vii) In every inside storage room there
rules.quote: (vii) In every inside storage room there shall be maintained one clear aisle at least 3 feet wide.

rules.subject: (viii) The cushion part of the body belt
rules.quote: (viii) The cushion part of the body belt shall contain no exposed rivets on the inside and shall be at least 76 millimeters (3 inches) in width.

rules.subject: (x) Locks on caissons
rules.quote: (x) Locks on caissons shall be so located that the bottom door shall be not less than 3 feet above the water level surrounding the caisson on the outside. (The water level, where it is affected by tides, is construed to mean high tide.).

rules.subject: (x) Repair bracket scaffolds. (1) Brackets
rules.quote: (x) Repair bracket scaffolds. (1) Brackets shall be secured in place by at least one wire rope at least 1/2 inch (1.27 cm) in diameter.
